facts.statement: cite a source for each important claim, listed in a "References" section at the bottom of the post
spelling and grammar are the only fixes applied directly; everything else goes in the report as proposals
flag statements with ambiguous subjects or referents
propose illustrations and analogies to explain complex concepts
show good and bad examples side by side, each with a caption explaining why
propose a call-out quote for the start of every section
a paraphrased or synthesized quote is acceptable when no single sentence covers it
repetition is acceptable only when important enough to drill, relevant in each section, and worded differently each time
`> EDITOR:` lines are direct author requests; resolve each and remove/rewrite the marker
flag any link not written as `[label](url)`
flag multi-line code-block lines longer than 80 characters
the 80-character limit applies to code blocks only, not blockquotes or other preformatted elements
report uses numbered sections with lettered items (1.a, 1.b, ...)
every proposed fix includes an example or concrete suggestion
reference locations by description or quoted snippet, never line numbers
a claim matching the repository's documents can still be wrong; check external sources for externally verifiable claims
evaluate every occurrence of a repeated concept separately; do not stop at the first

excluded.reason: frontmatter-convention guidance is always out of scope
restatements of workflow facts already inventoried
